Machine-learning methods are often described as assumption-free. They are not. They
make fewer assumptions about the *shape* of relationships than a linear model does,
which is a real advantage. But they make strong assumptions about how the data were
collected, and marine data violates most of them.

Two stations ten metres apart are not independent observations. A time series sampled
monthly for three years tells you little about a decadal cycle. Survey effort follows
ports, weather windows and funding. Predicting into unsampled depth or an unprecedented
temperature is extrapolation, whatever the model's confidence output says.

This is the section that determines whether the rest of the course helps you or
misleads you.

## Findings from this section

- 720 survey visits turned out to be worth **549** independent observations. One
  coefficient's honest standard error was **2.77 times** the naive one, and a fabricated
  site-level variable went from *p* = 0.09 to *p* = 0.19.
- A flexible model recovered the true temperature optimum almost exactly, 9.30 °C against
  a true 9, and put the depth optimum at **15 m where the truth is 80 m**. Same method,
  same data, same flexibility. The difference was confounding.
- A Poisson model of these counts expects 68 empty stations where **159** were observed,
  and its standard errors are too small by a factor of **1.9**, which moves three terms
  from *p* < 0.01 to *p* > 0.05.
- A random forest using **only longitude and latitude** scored R² 0.075 under random
  cross-validation and **0.011** under spatially blocked folds.
- Asked to predict below 100 m having trained above it, a random forest over-predicted by
  **73%**, against models biased by 2–8% in range.
- Downsampling, upsampling and SMOTE **moved along** the sensitivity–specificity curve
  rather than lifting it; upsampling matched simply setting the threshold to the
  prevalence.

::: {.callout-important}
If observations are spatially or temporally dependent, ordinary cross-validation will
overstate performance, sometimes dramatically. The fix is in
[7 · Validation](../07-validation/index.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Three of these pages compare models across *different* test sets, and each one notes that
**RMSE is not comparable between resampling schemes**, because different folds hold different
distributions of the response. Use R², or the same test set for both. It is the single
most repeated methodological trap in the course.
:::


## Further resources

**Documentation**

- [spatialsample](https://spatialsample.tidymodels.org/), tidymodels. Blocked, clustered and buffered resampling for data with a location, which is the concrete answer to most of this section.
- [Common pitfalls and recommended practices](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html), scikit-learn. Independence is assumed silently in almost every default, and this page says where.
